summary: Native N-API addon harvests browser cookies and stored logins on require()
details: The package ships a single ~10 MB Rust-built Linux N-API binary (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`) set as `main`, so its native code executes as soon as any consumer runs `require()` on the package. Embedded strings in the binary include Chrome/Chromium `Cookies` SQLite schema DDL (`cookies_unique_index ON cookies(host_key, top_frame_site_key,...)`), a `Found login for` label, `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER`, and a `Cookie.value when inserting` message — the fingerprint of a browser cookie and stored-login stealer that reads Chrome/Chromium credential stores on the installer's host. The same binary statically links a full outbound HTTP/HTTPS + TLS stack (hyper, ureq, rustls), ZSTD and zip compression, and proxy environment awareness (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`), providing the compress-and-POST-over-TLS exfiltration channel for the harvested credentials, including through enterprise egress proxies. The package name `new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu` mimics the platform-suffix naming of legitimate napi-rs prebuild artifacts, and the version `3.1.41-browser-release-151-upd-native-tools-397-1785772979` is a fabricated pre-release tag with a numeric epoch suffix rather than a normal semver release. No source, no repository, no author metadata, and no JavaScript wrapper are shipped — only the opaque native binary that runs at require-time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
